extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark of 1,825 diverse tasks for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual code generation across nine domains (e.g., web applications, games, SVG generation, simulations). It uses an automated multimodal evaluation pipeline that renders artifacts, captures three-step screenshots of dynamic behavior, and scores outputs using an MLLM-as-Judge guided by fine-grained per-task checklists.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters were applied, followed by de-duplication, prompt rewriting by experts and LLMs, difficulty calibration using 30+ models, checklist generation with human refinement, and solvability validation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots, covering nine primary topics: Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications, Simulations, Data Science, Management Systems, Multimedia Editing, Quick Tools, and Others.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts with front-end development experience independently scored 280 randomly selected queries from 6 models under a double-blind protocol (annotators unaware of MLLM scores, samples in randomized order). Final human ground-truth score is the median of individual annotators' ratings. Checklists were LLM-drafted and then human-refined; a 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration. Sub-categories tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators on the 10% manually curated seed. Pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) computed between automated referee and human experts across 280-instance, six-model human study, targeting >90% pairwise agreement.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple annotators per item (exact number not specified); final score is the median of individual annotators' ratings.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Engineers with extensive front-end development experience.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLM-based checklist drafting (Hunyuan-Turbos); lightweight classifier for sub-category tagging; LLM rewriting for prompt diversity; automated MLLM-as-Judge using Qwen2.5-VL-72B and Gemini-2.5-Pro as dual referees.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark evaluates dynamic behavior via discrete screenshot sampling at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. It also focuses only on single-turn artifact generation and does not assess agentic or iterative development capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of LLMs on dynamic visual artifact generation tasks, including testing and comparison of model capabilities across difficulty tiers and artifact types.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released. Future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication filtering using MinHash + semantic similarity and screenshot perceptual hashing; difficulty calibration enforcing 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split based on aggregated performance of 30+ models; prompt rewriting by experts and LLMs for diverse styles; checklist calibration using a 10% manually curated seed achieving Cohen's κ ≥0.8; solvability validation pruning underspecified or brittle items.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items; experts rewrite prompts for clarity/completeness/executability; sub-categories tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks; standardized execution with headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024×768 resolution with deterministic seeds; three staged screenshots captured per artifact to summarize interaction trajectories.

name.evidence: we introduce ArtifactsBench, a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation.

description.evidence: We curate 1,825 diverse tasks and evaluate over 30 leading LLMs. Our framework renders each artifact and captures its dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots. This visual evidence, alongside the source code, is then assessed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge, which is rigorously guided by a fine-grained, per-task checklist to ensure holistic and reproducible scoring.

url.evidence: We opensource ArtifactsBench, including the benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io

isLiveDataset.evidence: We curate 1,825 diverse tasks via a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We aggregate candidates from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We aggregate candidates from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots... Experts rewrite for clarity/completeness/executability; LLM rewriting adds diverse styles; humans verify.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We aggregate candidates from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots... ArtifactsBench comprises 1,825 executable queries covering nine primary topics.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We randomly selected 280 queries, along with the corresponding data from 6 models, and have them independently scored by multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience. The process follows a double-blind protocol: annotators remain unaware of the MLLM's scores, and the samples appear in randomized order to mitigate bias. The final human ground-truth score represents the median of the individual annotators' ratings.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration and achieves Cohen's κ ≥0.8 among annotators... we first validate the automatic referee via a 280-instance, six-model human study, demonstrating high pairwise agreement (targeting >90%)

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: The final human ground-truth score represents the median of the individual annotators' ratings.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: independently scored by multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Checklists are generated by Hunyuan-Turbos and human-refined... Sub-categories are tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks... we adopt a dual-referee setup: the open-source Qwen2.5-VL-72B and the proprietary Gemini-2.5-Pro.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: for highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions (e.g., multi-step user workflows in a web application, or the nuanced physics in a game), this discrete sampling may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of the entire interactive experience... ArtifactsBench currently focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn from a given prompt.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present ArtifactsBench, an automated benchmark for evaluating LLMs on dynamic visual artifacts, addressing static/non-visual gaps. Contributions: (i) a diverse, difficulty-calibrated set of 1,825 tasks; (ii) an automated, checklist-guided MLLM referee scoring code, visuals, and interaction.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings; future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Two-stage filtering: (i) MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts... Difficulty is assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce 30%/40%/30%... A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration and achieves Cohen's κ ≥0.8 among annotators... Tasks solved only by brittle hacks (e.g., hard-coded coordinates that break under minor viewport changes) are revised or removed.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Automated filters drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics... Experts rewrite for clarity/completeness/executability; LLM rewriting adds diverse styles; humans verify... Sub-categories are tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks... We standardize execution with headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024 × 768 resolution and deterministic seeds. We capture three staged screenshots (before/during/after scripted interaction).
